questions.prompt: payments-api's catalog-info.yaml says dependsOn: [resource:payments-db]. The payments-db descriptor says nothing about payments-api. Can the catalog answer "what depends on payments-db"?
choices: No: only the side that declares the dependency knows about it
Only if payments-db also lists dependencyOf: [component:payments-api]
Yes: the catalog stores the relation in both directions, dependsOn on payments-api and dependencyOf on payments-db
Only through a full-text search for the string payments-db
questions.explanation: The catalog derives a pair of relations from each reference: the declaring entity gets dependsOn and the target gets dependencyOf. Only one side writes YAML; both sides can be queried.

questions.prompt: A Component in metadata.namespace: payments has spec.owner: payments-team. The team is defined as a Group named payments-team with no namespace. What does the catalog do?
choices: It resolves the owner to group:payments/payments-team, which does not exist, so the component is accepted with an owner that points nowhere
It rejects the component because the owner does not exist
It resolves the owner to group:default/payments-team, because references default to the default namespace
It searches every namespace for a group called payments-team
questions.explanation: A reference without a namespace inherits the referring entity's namespace. Existence is not checked at validation time, so the entity is accepted and the ownership edge is broken; only a broken-reference check finds it. Write owner: group:default/payments-team.

questions.prompt: fx-rates declares spec.owner: system:payments. It passes validation. What does the catalog show as its owner?
choices: The payments System, which counts as owner
The owner of the payments System, inherited automatically
An error, because owner must be a Group
Nothing: ownedBy only accepts a Group or User, so the relation is dropped and the owner field is empty
questions.explanation: The owner field's allowed kinds are Group and User. The reference parses, so the entity is valid, but the model-driven processor emits no ownedBy relation for a System. minicatalog reports it as a dropped relation so it does not go unnoticed.

questions.prompt: A scorecard has bronze (owner, system), silver (runbook, on-call) and gold (SLO, docs, current template). A service passes owner, system, on-call, SLO, docs and the template rule, but has no runbook link. What level does it reach?
choices: Gold, because six of seven rules pass
Bronze, because a level needs every rule of that level and of all levels below it
Silver, because on-call passes
None, because one rule failed
questions.explanation: Levels are cumulative gates. The missing runbook fails silver, so the service stays at bronze whatever its score. That is why a CI gate should check the level, not the percentage.

questions.prompt: Yesterday's export had component:default/legacy-billing from payments-api/catalog-info.yaml. Today that file is still registered but no longer contains the entity. What is legacy-billing now?
choices: Deleted automatically with the next refresh, in every configuration
A conflict, because two files defined it
A broken reference
An orphan: its source no longer produces it, so Backstage marks it backstage.io/orphan and keeps it unless orphans are configured to be deleted
questions.explanation: An orphan is an entity whose parent no longer emits it. Backstage keeps orphans by default so that a bad commit does not delete half the catalog, and flags them so someone can unregister them or restore the descriptor.

questions.prompt: payments-db goes down. payments-api depends on it and provides the payments-api API, which checkout-web consumes. Which walk finds checkout-web?
choices: ownedBy from payments-db to its team, then ownerOf
dependsOn from payments-db
dependencyOf from payments-db to payments-api, providesApi to the API, then apiConsumedBy to checkout-web
partOf from payments-db to its System, then hasPart
questions.explanation: The blast radius follows reverse dependency edges: who depends on me (dependencyOf), which APIs those dependents provide (providesApi) and who consumes them (apiConsumedBy). Walking the System would list everything in it, including entities that keep working.
